title: Rebuild of burned 1429 Front Street home deferred
summary: On October 6, the board deferred its design review of a proposal to rebuild a home at 1429 Front Street, which burned in the Lāhainā fire, until more accurate drawings are ready; the owner said he will have them redone. 2 feet) and the drawings put the 40-foot shoreline setback line through the main house, so a setback variance is needed, which the Maui Planning Commission will decide.

timeline.text: The chair said the board looks forward to seeing the project back in the future.
The board voted to defer, or postpone, its review until more accurate drawings are ready.
The owner said he will make sure the drawings are redone.
The chair said one plan sheet shows the home at 10.2 feet above sea level, but the owner described 14.2 feet.
The owner said he was told in writing that the county sewer line would not be extended down Front Street.
The planner said the Maui Planning Commission will decide whether to grant the variance (an exception to the rules).
The planner said the setback variance is a discretionary permit the Maui Planning Commission could vote down or change.
A board member said the drawings did not show the building outside the 40-foot shoreline setback (the required distance from the shoreline).
The planner said the on-site wastewater system pushes the home past what shoreline rules allow, so a variance is needed.
Staff said a new on-site wastewater system must go in the corner where parking will be, which limits where the house can sit.
The owner plans to raise the home above flood level plus 3.2 feet for projected sea level rise and one foot more.
Staff said the board's design recommendations on the second item go to the Maui Planning Commission, which will take public testimony at a future date.
The second item was a home at 1429 Front Street that burned in the Lāhainā fire and is being rebuilt.
The second project also asks for a shoreline setback variance, which is permission to build closer to the ocean than rules allow.
The board voted to approve the rebuild design.
The chair said the board had no comments or recommendations on the rebuild.
The applicant said the new home is under the 3,500 square foot maximum.
The applicant said the number of bedrooms and bathrooms matches the home that was lost.
The applicant said the ʻohana now sits above the garage to stay outside the shoreline setback.
Staff said the board's recommendations on the rebuild go to the Maui Planning Commission.
